newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Index expiry fails to get FTSE 100 to 4000.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Index expiry fails to get FTSE 100 to 4000.

text.p: The expiration of September FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 futures, along September FTSE options, provided for a volatile morning session on Friday, that saw the leading index narrowly miss 4,000 mark that so many traders had been targeting.
By 1233 GMT, the FTSE 100 was off 8.0 points at 3,966.3, after jumping to a record peak of 3,994.1 ahead of expiration and then sinking to the day's low at 3,964.4.
High volume in September 4,000 calls all week and the big build-up of opening interest in those calls suggested to some that expiry would help drive the index over 4,000, dealers said.
Volume was heaviest in the September 4,000 calls again today, totalling a hefty 10,432 contracts.
Traders also noted large open interest in the Euro-FTSE 4,025 calls, as well.

"Getting through 4,000 on expiry was what everyone was talking about," said one options dealer. "There was a squeeze in September futures to get them above 4,000. They massaged the market higher ahead of expiration expecting to push it further on expiry. But institutions sold into it."
September FTSE 100 futures went out at an official 3,978, well off their high of 4,000 met just before expiration.
Trading equity options was overshadowed by expiration of index derivatives, dealers said.
"Everyone was soley focused on expiration," a dealer said. "Now there are quite a lot of people nursing their wounds."

Among the few big trades recorded in stock options was the sale of 300 November 260 calls on BTR Plc at 22p. The sale was related to dividend stripping, as the industrial conglomerate is due to go ex-dividend on Monday, dealers said.
Shares in BTR were up 1-1/2p to 282p.
They noted the sale of 400 November 280 calls in BTR at 8p, but that trade was not linked to the payout, they said.
